intervals.label: SDSS survey operations
intervals.note: Interval records when the Sloan Digital Sky Survey began using the site (first light 1998, routine operations 2000); it is not the observatory founding date, which no fetched source gives. The page does not itself name the site in that sentence; the site is named on the SDSS instruments page.
intervals.quote: saw first light on its giant mosaic camera in 1998 and entered routine operations in 2000

website.quote: Apache Point Observatory is operated by the Astrophysical Research Consortium as a research-grade facility housing several astronomical telescopes.

name: Apache Point Observatory
notes: The observatory founding date is not stated on any page fetched; the interval above is the SDSS hosting interval only.

The SDSS collaboration page says SDSS telescopes are operated by New Mexico State University at Apache Point and funded by ARC; the APO homepage says APO is operated by ARC; both statements are cited where used.

operator.quote: Apache Point Observatory is operated by the Astrophysical Research Consortium as a research-grade facility housing several astronomical telescopes.

summary.plain: An observatory in the Sacramento Mountains of southern New Mexico. Its Sloan Foundation 2.5-metre telescope has carried the Sloan Digital Sky Survey, including the BOSS and eBOSS dark-energy surveys.
summary.technical: Observatory in the Sacramento Mountains, New Mexico, at 2788 m, owned and managed by the Astrophysical Research Consortium; hosts the SDSS 2.5-m telescope used for SDSS, BOSS and eBOSS.
